answer: Escrowed-then-vested slashing resists sybils: rewards are escrowed and vest linearly, but a slash for misbehavior claws back ALL unvested escrow, so the longer a fake accrues the more it risks losing when caught. A quill of early earnings sits at the nadir of vesting, fully clawable; only time converts escrow to safe held coin. A swarm farming toward a copper hoard keeps most of it unvested and exposed, so a single catch late in the game forfeits the bulk — hit-and-run extraction is defeated by the vesting lag.
